arabicText: أنه سأل أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن رجل يجد في إانئه افرة، وقد توضأ من ذلك اإلانء مرارا، أو إغتسل منه، أو غسل ثيابه، وقد كانت الفارة متسلخة، فقال: إن كان رآها في اإلانء قبل أن يغتسل أو يتوضأ أو يغسل ثيابه، ثم فعل ذلك بعد ما رآها في اإلانء، فعليه أن يغسل ثيابه ويغسل كل ما أصابه ذلك الماء ويعيد الوضوء والصالة. وإن كان إنما رآها بعد ما فرغ من ذلك وفعله فال يمس من ذلك الماء شيئا، وليس عليه شئ، ألنه ال يعلم متى سقطت فيه، ثم اقل: لعله أن يكون إنما سقطت فيه تلك الساعة التي رآها.
englishText: Based on his asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who finds a mouse in his vessel, and he had performed ablution from that vessel multiple times, or performed ghusl from it, or washed his clothes, and the mouse was decomposed. He said: If he saw it in the vessel before performing ghusl or ablution or washing his clothes, then did these after seeing it in the vessel, he must wash his clothes and wash everything that water touched and repeat the ablution and prayer. However if he only saw it after finishing all that and doing it, then he shouldn't touch anything from that water, and nothing is required of him, because he doesn't know when it fell in it. Then he said: Perhaps it only fell in it at that hour when he saw it.

chapter: Ruling On Water Being Pure Until Impurity Is Known To Have Affected It
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: الماء كله طاهر حتى تعلم أنه قذر.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: All water is pure until you know it is impure.

chapter: Flowing Water Does Not Become Impure Merely Upon Contact With Impurity Unless It Changes
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: ال أبس أبن يبول الرجل في الماء الجاري، وكره أن يبول في الماء الراكد.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem if a man urinates in flowing water, but it is disliked to urinate in stagnant water.

chapter: Flowing Water Does Not Become Impure Merely Upon Contact With Impurity Unless It Changes
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الرجل يبول في الماء الجاري؟ اقل: ال أبس به إذا كان الماء جاراي.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man urinating in flowing water? He said: There is no problem with it if the water is flowing.

chapter: Flowing Water Does Not Become Impure Merely Upon Contact With Impurity Unless It Changes
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: ال أبس ابلبول في الماء الجاري.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with urinating in flowing water.

chapter: Flowing Water Does Not Become Impure Merely Upon Contact With Impurity Unless It Changes
arabicText: سألته عن الماء الجاري يبال فيه؟ اقل: ال أبس به.
englishText: I asked him about urinating in flowing water? He said: There is no problem with it.

chapter: Flowing Water Does Not Become Impure Merely Upon Contact With Impurity Unless It Changes
arabicText: سألته عن الرجل يمر ابلميتة في الماء؟ اقل: يتوضأ من الناحية التي ليس فيها الميتة.
englishText: I asked him about a man who passes by a dead animal in water? He said: He should perform ablution from the side where there is no dead animal. Shaykh Hurr Amili: A group of our scholars have interpreted this to apply to flowing water and a large quantity (Kurr) of stagnant water, and what indicates this will be mentioned.

chapter: Flowing Water Does Not Become Impure Merely Upon Contact With Impurity Unless It Changes
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: لو أن ميزابين ساال، أحدهما ميزاب بول، واآلخر ميزاب ماء افختلطا ثم أصابك، ما كان به أبس.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: If two spouts were flowing, one of them a spout of urine and the other a spout of water, and they mixed then touched you, there would be no problem with it. Shaykh Hurr Amili: Even though the water here is considered absolute, the strongest cases and the most fitting for this ruling is running water, and what indicates this will be mentioned in narrations about bath water, rainwater, well water, and others. Flowing Water Does Not Become Impure Merely Upon Contact With Impur...

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: عن هشام بن سالم أنه سأل أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن السطح يبال عليه، فتصيبه السماء فيكف فيصيب الثوب؟ فقال: ال أبس به، ما أصابه من الماء أكثر منه.
englishText: From Hisham ibn Salim, who asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about urinating on a roof, then rain falls on it and drips, then it touches clothing? He said: There is no harm in it, as long as the water that touches it is more than the urine.

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: سألته عن البيت يبال عىل ظهره، ويغتسل من الجنابة ثم يصيبه المطر، أيؤخذ من مائه فيتوضأ به للصالة؟ فقال: إذا جرى فال أبس به. وسألته عن الرجل يمر في ماء المطر وقد صب فيه خمر، أفصاب ثوبه، هل يصيل فيه قبل أن يغسله؟ فقال: ال يغسل ثوبه وال رجله، ويصيل فيه وال أبس به.
englishText: I asked him about a house on whose roof someone urinates and performs the major ablution for sexual impurity, then rain falls on it. Can water be taken from it to perform ablution for prayer? He said: If it flows, there is no problem with it. I asked him about a man who passes through rainwater into which wine has been poured, and it touches his garment. Can he pray in it before washing it? He said: He does not need to wash his garment or his foot, and he can pray in it without any problem.

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: عن عبد هللا بن الحسن، عن جده عيل بن جعفر، مثله. وزاد: وسألته عن الكنيف يكون فوق البيت فيصيبه المطر فيكف، فيصيب الثياب، أيصىل فيها قبل أن تغسل؟ اقل: إذا جرى من ماء المطر فال أبس.
englishText: From Abdullah bin Al-Hasan, from his grandfather Ali bin Ja'far, similar to it. He added: And I asked him about a latrine that is on top of the house, and it gets rained on and leaks, then it touches the clothes. Can one pray in them before washing them? He said: If it flows from rainwater, then there is no problem.

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم)، في ميزابين ساال، أحدهما بول واآلخر ماء المطر افختلطا أفصاب ثوب رجل لم يضره ذلك.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding two spouts flowing, one of urine and the other of rainwater, which mixed and then touched a man's garment: it does not harm him.

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) - في حديث - اقل: قلت: يسيل عيل من ماء المطر أرى فيه التغير، وأرى فيه آاثر القذر، فتقطر القطرات عىل، وينتضح عيل منه والبيت يتوضأ عىل سطحه، فيكف عىل ثيابنا؟ اقل: ما بذا أبس، ال تغسله كل شئ يراه ماء المطر فقد طهر. أقول: هذا محمول عىل أن القطرات، وما وصل إلى الثياب، من غير الناحية التي فيها التغير، وآاثر القذر، لما مر. أو أن التغير بغير النجاسة، والقذر بمعنى الوسخ ويخص بغير النجاسة.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) - in a hadith - he said: I said: Water from rain flows upon me and I see change in it, and I see traces of dirt in it, and drops fall on me, and it splashes on me, and people perform ablution on the house's roof, so it drips on our clothes? He said: There is no harm in this, do not wash it, everything that rain water touches becomes pure. I (Hurr Amili) say: This is interpreted to mean that the droplets and what reaches the clothes from directions other than where there is change and traces of filth, based on what was previously mentioned. Or that the change is due to something other than impurity, and filth here means dirt specifically other than ritual impurity.

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: عن أبي الحسن (عليه السالم)، في طين المطر، أنه ال أبس به أن يصيب الثوب ثالثة أايم، إال أن يعلم أنه قد نجسه شئ بعد المطر.
englishText: From Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding mud from rain, there is no harm if it touches the garment for three days, unless it is known that something has made it impure after the rain.

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: سئل - يعني الصادق (عليه السالم) - عن طين المطر يصيب الثوب فيه البول، والعذرة، والدم؟ فقال: طين المطر ال ينجس.
englishText: The question was posed to al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, about the mud from rain coming into contact with clothes that have urine, excrement, and blood on them? He said: The mud from rain does not become impure. Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into C... Shaykh Hurr Amili: This is specific to the time of the rain's descent, or to the removal of impurity during the rain.

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: سألت أاب (عبد هللا عليه) السالم عن الكنيف يكون خارجا، فتمطر السماء، فتقطر عيل القطرة؟ اقل: ليس به أبس.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, about an outhouse that is outside, and when it rains, a drop falls on me? He said: There is no harm in it.

chapter: Rainwater Not Becoming Impure Upon Falling, Merely By Coming Into Contact With Impurity
arabicText: عيل بن جعفر في كتابه، عن أخيه موسى عليه السالم اقل: سألته عن المطر يجري في المكان فيه العذرة، فيصيب الثوب، أيصىل فيه قبل أن يغسل؟ اقل: إذا جرى به المطر فال أبس.
englishText: Ali ibn Ja'far in his book, from his brother Musa, peace be upon him, said: I asked him about rain flowing in a place containing excrement, and it touches the garment. Can one pray in it before washing it? He said: If the rain has flowed over it, then there is no problem.

chapter: Water Of Bathhouse Is Not Impure When It Has A Source Despite Contact With Impurities
arabicText: قلت ألبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم): ما تقول في ماء الحمام؟ اقل: هو بمنزلة الماء الجاري.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): What do you say about the water of the bathhouse? He said: It is like flowing water.

chapter: Water Of Bathhouse Is Not Impure When It Has A Source Despite Contact With Impurities
arabicText: قلت ألبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم): الحمام يغتسل فيه الجنب وغيره، أغتسل من مائه؟ اقل: نعم، ال أبس أن يغتسل منه الجنب، ولقد اغتسلت فيه، ثم جئت فغسلت رجيل، وما غسلتهما إال مما لزق بهما من التراب.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): The bathhouse where the ritually impure and others bathe, can I perform ghusl with its water? He said: Yes, there is no problem for the ritually impure person to perform ghusl from it. I have performed ghusl in it myself, then I came and washed my feet, and I only washed them because of the dirt that stuck to them.

chapter: Water Of Bathhouse Is Not Impure When It Has A Source Despite Contact With Impurities
arabicText: اقل: رأيت أاب جعفر (عليه السالم) جائيا من الحمام وبينه وبين داره قذر، فقال: لوال ما بيني وبين داري ما غسلت رجيل، وال نحيت ماء الحمام.
englishText: From Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) coming from the bathhouse and between him and his house was some filth. He said: If not for what is between me and my house, I would not have washed my feet, nor would I have removed the bathhouse water.

chapter: Water Of Bathhouse Is Not Impure When It Has A Source Despite Contact With Impurities
arabicText: عن أبي جعفر (عليه السالم) اقل: ماء الحمام ال أبس به إذا كانت له مادة.
englishText: From Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: There is no harm in the bathhouse water if it has a source.

chapter: Water Of Bathhouse Is Not Impure When It Has A Source Despite Contact With Impurities
arabicText: سألته عن ماء الحمام؟ فقال: أدخله بإزار، وال تغتسل من ماء آخر، إال أن يكون فيهم (١) جنب، أو يكثر أهله فال يدرى فيهم جنب أم ال.
englishText: I asked him about bathhouse water? He said: Enter it with a waist wrap, and do not perform ghusl from the used water, unless there is someone in state of ritual impurity among them, or if there are many people and it is not known if there is someone in state of ritual impurity among them or not. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The Sheikh interpreted it as referring to the absence of a source, and closer to it is interpreting it as allowing bathing with other than its water then, and the removal of the undesirability of bathing with another water. Indeed, this is exactly what it indicates, as there is no indication of impurity that would necessitate interpretation, mentioned by the author of AlMuntaqa, and others.

chapter: Water Of Bathhouse Is Not Impure When It Has A Source Despite Contact With Impurities
arabicText: سئل عن الرجال يقومون عىل الحوض في الحمام، ال أعرف اليهودي من النصراني، وال الجنب من غير الجنب؟ اقل: تغتسل منه، وال تغتسل من ماء آخر إفنه طهور.
englishText: He was asked about men standing at the pool in the bathhouse, where one cannot distinguish a Jew from a Christian, nor one who is in ritual impurity from one who is not? He said: Perform ablution from it, and do not perform ablution from other water for it is purifying.

chapter: Water Of Bathhouse Is Not Impure When It Has A Source Despite Contact With Impurities
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: قلت: أخبرني عن ماء الحمام، يغتسل منه، الجنب، والصبي، واليهودي، والنصراني، والمجوسي؟ فقال: إن ماء الحمام كماء النهر يطهر بعضه بعضا.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: I said: Tell me about the water of the bathhouse, from which the ritually impure, children, Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians perform ablution? He said: Indeed the water of the bathhouse is like river water - parts of it purify other parts.

chapter: Water Of Bathhouse Is Not Impure When It Has A Source Despite Contact With Impurities
arabicText: عن أبي الحسن األول (عليه السالم)، اقل: ماء الحمام ال ينجسه شئ.
englishText: From Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him), he said: Nothing can make the water of the bathhouse impure.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: عن عيل بن جعفر، عن أخيه أبي الحسن موسى بن جعفر (عليه السالم) اقل: سألته عن جل رعف افمتخط، فصار بعض ذلك الدم قطعرا صغارا، أفصاب إانءه، هل يصلح له الوضوء منه؟ فقال: إن لم يكن شيئا يستبين في الماء فال أبس، وإن كان شيئا بينا فال تتوضأ منه. اقل وسألته عن رجل رعف وهو يتوضأ فتقطر قطرة في إانئه، هل يصلح الوضوء منه؟ اقل: ال.
englishText: From Ali bin Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan Musa bin Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him about a man who had a nosebleed and blew his nose, and some of that blood became small pieces that fell into his vessel. Is it permissible for him to perform ablution from it? He said: If it's not visibly apparent in the water, then there's no problem. But if it's clearly visible, then don't perform ablution from it. He said: And I asked him about a man who had a nosebleed while performing ablution, and a drop fell into his vessel. Is it permissible to perform ablution from it? He said: No. Translator: In the margin of the original manuscript (from him, may his grave be sanctified), it states: Some have assumed that it indicates the non-impurity of water with an amount of blood that is not perceptible. The truth is that there is no indication in it, as understood by later scholars, and we have mentioned it. Some have disputed its indication of impurity and the indication of similar narrations due to the absence of the term 'impurity,' which is far-fetched, because most of the hadiths on impurities are like this and do not go beyond these expressions. Moreover, the content of the chapter is agreed upon among the companions except for Abu Aqeel. These hadiths are also supported by what will come, along with the contradiction of taqiyyah, agreement with precaution, consensus, and other factors. Furthermore, the hadiths on the impurity of water due to change do not contain the term 'impurity').

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن رجل معه إانءان فيهما ماء وقع في أحدهما قذر ال يدري أيهما هو، وليس يقدر عىل ماء غيره؟ اقل: يهريقهما جميعا ويتيمم.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who has two containers with water, and something impure has fallen into one of them, but he doesn't know which one, and he has no access to any other water. He said: He should pour out both of them and perform tayammum (dry ablution).

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) - في الرجل الجنب يسهو فيغمس يده في اإلانء قبل أن يغسلها :- إنه ال أبس إذا لم يكن أصاب يده شئ.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) - regarding a person in a state of major ritual impurity who forgetfully dips his hand in a vessel before washing it -: There is no harm if nothing has contaminated his hand.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: عنهم (عليهم السالم) اقل: إذا أدخلت يدك في اإلانء قبل أن تغسلها فال أبس، إال أن يكون أصابها قذر بول أو جنابة، إفن أدخلت يدك في الماء وفيها شئ من ذلك أفهرق ذلك الماء.
englishText: From them (peace be upon them), they said: If you put your hand in a vessel before washing it, there is no harm, unless it has been affected by the filth of urine or ritual impurity. If you put your hand in the water while it has any of that on it, then pour out that water.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم)، عن الرجل الجنب ينتهي إلى الماء القليل في الطريق، ويريد أن يغتسل منه وليس معه إانء يغرف به ويداه قذراتن؟ اقل: يضع يده، ثم يتوضأ ، ثم يغتسل، هذا مما اقل هللا عز وجل: (ما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man in the state of ritual impurity who comes across a small amount of water on the path and wants to perform ghusl from it, but he does not have a vessel to scoop with and his hands are dirty? He said: He puts his hand in it, then performs wudu, then performs ghusl. This is from what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has said: [Allah has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty] [Quran, 22:78]. Shaykh Hurr Amili: And the Sheikh narrated it with his chain from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub. I say: This is susceptible to taqiyyah, so it does not oppose what was mentioned before and what comes after, and the indication of taqiyyah is mentioning ablution along with the bath for Janabah, so it can be interpreted as taqiyyah, or that the meant by dirt is filth not impurity, or the meant by a small amount of water is what reaches a Kurr without increase, for it is considered small in common parlance."

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: سئل الصادق (عليه السالم) عن ماء شربت منه دجاجة؟ فقال: إن كان في منقارها قذر لم تتوضأ منه ولم تشرب، وإن لم يعلم في منقارها قذر توضأ منه واشرب.
englishText: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about water from which a chicken had drunk. He said: If there is filth in its beak, do not perform ablution from it and do not drink it, but if no filth is known to be in its beak, perform ablution from it and drink it.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: سألت أاب الحسن (عليه السالم) عن الرجل يدخل يده في اإلانء وهي قذرة؟ اقل: يكفئ اإلانء.
englishText: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who puts his dirty hand into a vessel? He said: He should overturn the vessel.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الجرة تسع مائة رطل من ماء، يقع فيها أوقية من دم أشرب منه وأتوضأ؟ اقل: ال.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a jar containing nine hundred ratls of water, if an ounce of blood falls into it, can I drink from it and perform ablution? He said: No.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: إذا إن أصاب الرجل جنابة أفدخل يده في اإلانء فال أبس، إذا لم يكن أصاب يده شئ من المني.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: If a man becomes in a state of major ritual impurity and puts his hand into a vessel, there is no harm, provided his hand has not been touched by any semen.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: اقل: سألته عن رجل يمس الطست، أو الركوة ثم يدخل يده في اإلانء قبل أن يفرغ عىل كفيه؟ اقل: يهريق من الماء ثالث حفنات، وإن لم يفعل فال أبس، وإن كانت أصابته جنابة أفدخل يده في الماء فال أبس به إن لم يكن أصاب يده شئ من المني. وإن كان أصاب يده أفدخل يده في الماء قبل أن يفرغ عىل كفيه فليهرق الماء كله.
englishText: He said: I asked him about a man who touches a basin or a water container then puts his hand in the vessel before pouring water over his palms? He said: He should pour out three handfuls of water, and if he does not do so then there is no harm. And if he was in a state of major ritual impurity and put his hand in the water, there is no harm if no semen had touched his hand. But if semen had touched his hand and he put it in the water before pouring over his palms, then he should pour out all the water. Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact ...

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: سألته عن الجنب يحمل الركوة أو التور، فيدخل أصبعه فيه؟ اقل: وقل: إن كانت يده قذرة أفهرقه، وإن كان لم يصبها قذر فليغتسل منه. هذا مما اقل هللا تعالى: ما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him about a person in a state of major ritual impurity carrying a water container or a bowl, and if he can put his finger in it? He said: Say: If his hand is dirty, then pour it out, and if it has not been touched by dirt, then he may perform ghusl (ritual bath) with it. This is from what Allah Almighty said: He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: اقل: كنت مع أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) في حائط فحضرت الصالة فنزح دلوا للوضوء، من ريك له فخرج عليه قطعة عذرة ايبسة أفكفأ رأسه وتوضأ ابلباقي.
englishText: He said: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in a garden when the time for prayer came. He drew a bucket of water for ablution from his well, and a piece of dry excrement came up with it, so he poured out its top portion and performed ablution with the remaining water. Shaykh Hurr Amili: I interpret, the Sheikh considered it as feces from an animal whose meat is eaten, as it does not make the water impure. It may also be interpreted as taqiyyah, and that the remaining meant is what remained in the well, not in the bucket, and that the bucket was a Kurr (a large quantity of water), among other interpretations."

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: عن عيل بن جعفر عن أخيه موسى بن جعفر (عليه السالم) اقل: سألته عن الدجاجة والحمامة وأشباههما تطأ العذرة ثم تدخل في الماء يتوضأ منه للصالة؟ اقل: ال، إال أن يكون الماء كثيرا قدر كر من ماء.
englishText: From Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him about a chicken, a pigeon, and similar birds that step on feces and then enter water, can one perform ablution from that water for prayer? He said: No, unless the water is abundant, about the amount of a kurr of water.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) - في حديث - اقل سئل عن رجل معه إانءان فيهما ماء، وقع في أحدهما قذر ال يدري أيهما هو، (وحضرت الصالة)، وليس يقدر عىل ماء غيرهما؟ اقل: يهريقهما جميعا ويتيمم.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) - in a hadith - he said: He was asked about a man who has two containers with water, and some impurity fell into one of them, but he doesn't know which one, (and the time for prayer has come), and he has no access to any other water? He said: He should pour out both of them and perform tayammum.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: لما كان في الليلة التي وعد فيها عيل بن الحسين (عليه السالم) اقل لمحمد: اي بنى ابغني وضوءا، اقل: فقمت فجئته بماء. فقال ال تبغ هذا، إفن فيه شيئا ميتا. اقل فخرجت فجئت ابلمصباح إفذا فيفارة ميتة فجئته بوضوء غيره.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: During the night in which Ali bin Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was promised death, he said to Muhammad: O my son, bring me water for ablution. He said: I got up and brought him water. He said: Do not bring this, for there is something dead in it. He said: So I went out and brought a lamp, and there was a dead mouse in it, so I brought him different water for ablution.

chapter: Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact With Impurity, Even If It Does Not Change
arabicText: سألته عن جرة ماء فيه ألف رطل وقع فيه أوقية بول، هل يصلح شربه أو الوضوء منه؟ اقل: ال يصلح.
englishText: I asked him about a jug of water containing a thousand ratls (*) into which an ounce of urine had fallen, whether it was permissible to drink from it or perform ablution with it. He said: It is not permissible. Translator: * This is referring to the Iraqi definition of ratl and therefore the jar of water amounts to less than Kurr. See Hadith 416 for a definition of Kurr in Iraqi ratl. Shaykh Hurr Amili: And there comes what indicates this in the narrations about the Kurr and impurities, and containers, and the reasoning for washing the hands due to the possibility of impurity and other things which are very many. And there has been what appears to be contradictory, and there will come what seems so, which is general and subject to specification, or absolute and subject to restriction, along with the possibility of interpreting it as taqiyyah for its agreement with the doctrines of the A'ammah (general muslims) and its opposition to the consensus of the Shia, or what is famous among them, and it is only agreed upon by the rare and odd, along with the opposition to precaution, and other things. Impurity Of Stagnant Water Less Than A Kurr By Coming Into Contact ...

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) وسأل عن الماء تبول فيه الدواب وتلغ فيه الكالب، ويغتسل فيه الجنب؟ اقل: إذا كان الماء قدر كر لم ينجسه شئ.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he was asked about water in which animals urinate, dogs lap, and people in a state of major ritual impurity bathe. He said: If the water is the amount of a kurr, nothing can make it impure.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: إذا كان الماء قدر كر لم ينجسه شئ.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, who said: If the water is the amount of a kurr, nothing can make it impure.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم - في حديث - اقل: وال تشرب من سؤر الكلب إال أن يكون حوضا كبيرا يستقى منه.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) - in a hadith - he said: Do not drink from the leftover water of a dog unless it is from a large pond that people draw water from.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: عن عيل بن جعفر، عن أخيه موسى بن جعفر عليهما السالم اقل: سألته عن الدجاجة والحمامة وأشباههما تطأ العذرة ثم تدخل في الماء يتوضأ منه للصالة؟ اقل: ال، إال أن يكون الماء كثيرا قدر كر من ماء.
englishText: From Ali bin Ja'far, from his brother Musa bin Ja'far, peace be upon them both, who said: I asked him about a chicken, pigeon, and similar birds that step on feces then enter into water - can one perform ablution from it for prayer? He said: No, unless the water is abundant, approximately a kurr of water.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: قلت له: الغدير فيه ماء مجتمع تبول فيه الدواب وتلغ فيه الكالب، ويغتسل فيه الجنب؟ اقل: إذا كان قدر كر لم ينجسه شئ.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: The pond in which water is collected, where animals urinate in it, dogs lap from it, and the person in state of major ritual impurity performs ghusl in it? He said: If it reaches the amount of a kurr, nothing makes it impure.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: اقل سمعت أاب عبد هللا عليه السالم يقول: إذا كان الماء قدر كر لم ينجسه شئ.
englishText: He said: I heard Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, saying: If the water is the amount of a kurr, nothing can make it impure.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: اقل: سألت أاب عبد هللا عليه السالم عن الماء الذي ال ينجسه شئ؟ فقال: كر، قلت: وما الكر؟ اقل: ثالثة أشبار في ثالثة أشبار.
englishText: He said: I asked Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, about the water that nothing can pollute? He said: A kurr. I said: And what is a kurr? He said: Three spans by three spans.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: إذا كان الماء في الريك كرا لم ينجسه شئ، قلت: وكم الكر؟ اقل: في ثالثة أشبار ونصف عمقها، في ثالثة أشبار ونصف عرضها.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, who said: If the water in the well is a kurr, nothing can make it impure. I asked: And how much is a kurr? He said: Three and a half spans in depth, and three and a half spans in width. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The Sheikh interpreted it as taqiyyah due to the difference in ruling between a well and a pond, and it can be interpreted as referring to a non-spring well, for it is culturally considered a well, even if not legally so according to what will come, God willing, and the Sheikh also hinted at this.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: اقل: سئل الصادق عليه السالم عن الماء الساكن تكون فيه الجيفة؟ اقل: يتوضأ من الجانب اآلخر، وال يتوضأ من جانب الجيفة.
englishText: He said: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked about stagnant water that contains a carcass? He said: One should perform ablution from the other side, and not perform ablution from the side of the carcass. Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact Wit...

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: اقل: وأتى أهل البادية رسول هللا صىل هللا عليه وآله وسلم فقالوا: اي رسول هللا، إن حياضنا هذه تردها السباع، والكالب، والبهائم؟ فقال لهم صىل هللا عليه وآله وسلم: لها ما أخذت أفواهها ولكم سائر ذلك.
englishText: Bedouin people came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and said: O Messenger of Allah, these watering places of ours are frequented by predatory animals, dogs, and livestock? He, peace be upon him, said to them: What they drink with their mouths is for them, and the rest is for you. Shaykh Hurr Amili: This is interpreted as referring to the amount of a Kurr, because those ponds do not decrease from a Kurr, but rather mostly exceed it, as per what has passed and what will come."

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: أتيت أاب عبد هللا عليه السالم أسأله، افبتدأني، فقال: إن شئت فسل اي شهاب، وإن شئت أخبرانك بما جئت له، قلت: أخبرني، اقل: جئت تسألني عن الغدير يكون في جانبه الجيفة، أتوضأ منه أوال؟ اقل: نعم، اقل: توضأ من الجانب اآلخر، إال أن يغلب الماء الريح فينتن. وجئت تسأل عن الماء الراكد من الكر مما لم يكن فيه تغير أو ريح غالبة، قلت: فما التغير؟ اقل: الصفرة، فتوضأ منه، وكلما غلب عليه كثرة الماء فهو طاهر.
englishText: I came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) to ask him, and he began speaking before I did, saying: If you wish, ask O Shihab, and if you wish we will tell you what you came for. I said: Tell me. He said: You came to ask me about a pond that has a carcass on its side, whether to perform ablution from it or not? He said: Yes. He said: Perform ablution from the other side, unless the water is overcome by the odor and becomes putrid. And you came to ask about stagnant water that is kurr in amount where there is no change or dominant odor. I said: What is the change? He said: Yellowness. So perform ablution from it, and whenever the amount of water is abundant, it is pure.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الحياض التي ما بين مكة إلى المدينة تردها السباع، وتلغ فيها الكالب، وتشرب منها الحمير، ويغتسل فيها الجنب، ويتوضأ منه؟ اقل: وكم قدر الماء؟ اقل: إلى نصف الساق، وإلى الركبة، فقال: توضأ منه.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the watering pools between Makkah and Medina which predatory animals come to, and dogs lap from, and donkeys drink from, and the ritually impure person performs ghusl in, and performs ablution from it? He said: How much is the amount of water? He said: Up to half the shin, and up to the knee. He said: Perform ablution from it.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الماء الساكن واالستنجاء منه والجيفة فيه؟ فقال: توضأ من الجانب اآلخر، وال تتوضأ من جانب الجيفة.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about stagnant water, performing istinja (cleansing) from it, and the presence of a carcass in it? He said: Perform ablution from the other side, and do not perform ablution from the side where the carcass is.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: عن أبي بصير اقل: قلت ألبي عبد هللا عليه السالم إان نسافر، فربما بلينا ابلغدير من المطر يكون إلى جانب القرية، فتكون فيه العذرة، ويبول فيه الصبي، وتبول فيه الدابة، وتروث؟ فقال: إن عرض في قلبك منه شئ فقل هكذا، يعنى افرج الماء بيدك، ثم توضأ، إفن الدين ليس بمضيق، إفن هللا يقول: ما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج.
englishText: From Abu Basir who said: I said to Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him: We travel, and sometimes we come across a pond from rain water which is beside the village, and in it there is excrement, and children urinate in it, and animals urinate and defecate in it? He said: If something concerns you about it in your heart, then do like this - meaning part the water with your hand - then perform ablution, for indeed the religion is not restrictive, for Allah says: He has not placed upon you any hardship in religion [Quran, 22:78]. Shaykh Hurr Amili: Such a pond as mentioned likely exceeds a Kurr, or it is interpreted as referring to a Kurr, and it might be meant from the question during the rain as mentioned before."

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: كتبت إلى من يسأله عن الغدير، يجتمع فيه ماء السماء، ويستقى فيه من بئر، فيستنيج فيه اإلنسان من بول، أو يغتسل فيه الجنب، ما حده الذي ال يجوز؟ فكتب: ال توضأ من مثل هذا إال من ضرورة إليه. أقول: هذا محمول عىل بلوغ الكرية، واستحباب االجتناب مع عدم الضرورة، ولو لحصول النفرة بسبب االستنجاء.
englishText: I wrote to someone asking him about al-Ghadir (water pool), in which rainwater collects and water is drawn from a well, and in which a person performs istinja from urine, or a person in state of major impurity (janabah) performs ghusl, what is its limit that is not permissible? He wrote: Do not perform wudu from something like this except out of necessity. I (Hurr Amili) say: This is interpreted as referring to water reaching the volume of kurr, and the recommendation to avoid it when not necessary, even if only due to aversion caused by the istinja (cleansing). Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact Wit...

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: قلت ألبي عبد هللا عليه السالم: أكون في السفر أفتي الماء النقي ويدي قذرة، أفغمسها في الماء؟ اقل: ال أبس.
englishText: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): I am traveling and I come across clean water while my hands are dirty, can I immerse them in the water? He said: There is no problem. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The Sheikh said: This is meant if the water is a Kurr.

chapter: Non-impurity Of A Kurr Of Stagnant Water By Coming Into Contact With Impurity Without Change
arabicText: قلت ألبي عبد هللا عليه السالم: الرجل يضع الكوز الذي يغرف به من الحب في مكان قذر، ثم يدخله الحب؟ اقل: يصب من الماء ثالثة أكف، ثم يدلك الكوز.
englishText: I said to Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him: A man places the cup (or jug) which he uses to scoop from the water container in an unclean place, then puts it back into the water container? He said: Pour three handfuls of water [over it], then rub the cup. Shaykh Hurr Amili: It's possible that the grain is considered a Kurr (a large amount), and it might be meant by his saying "then enters it into the grain" to imply intending to enter it into the grain, as in the verse of Allah: "When you stand for prayer, wash your faces," etc., meaning: wash the scoop first before entering it into the grain, by the necessity of rubbing, and it can be interpreted as taqiyyah, and it might mean dirtiness rather than impurity.

chapter: Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)
arabicText: قلت ألبى عبد هللا عليه السالم) الماء الذي ال ينجسه شئ؟ اقل: ذراعان عمقه في ذراع وشبر وسعته.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): What amount of water does nothing make impure? He said: Two cubits in depth by one cubit and a span in width. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The intended width is each of the length and the width, so it considers four cubits in depth, and three in length, and three in width, as will come in the hadiths of the measurements that by cubit is meant two feet.

chapter: Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)
arabicText: محمد بن عيل بن الحسين في (المجالس) اقل: روى أن الكر هو ما يكون ثالثة أشبار طوال، في ثالثة أشبار عرضا، في ثالثة أشبار عمقا.
englishText: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Husayn said in (Al-Majalis): It is narrated that the Kurr is what measures three spans in length, by three spans in width, by three spans in depth.

chapter: Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)
arabicText: وفي كتاب (المقنع) اقل: روى أن الكر ذراعان وشبر في ذراعين وشبر.
englishText: And in the book (Al-Muqni') he said: It is narrated that the Kurr is two cubits and a span by two cubits and a span. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The cubit referred to here can mean the bone of the arm, which is slightly more than a span, thus making it consistent with the narration of Abu Basir.

chapter: Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم قلت: وما الكر؟ اقل: ثالثة أشبار في ثالثة أشبار.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), I said: What is the Kurr? He said: Three spans by three spans. Shaykh Hurr Amili: What is meant by one dimension is the depth, and by the other, both the length and the width, so it is consistent with the narration in "Al-Majalis."

chapter: Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: قلت: وكم الكر؟ اقل ثالثة أشبار ونصف عمقها، في ثالثة أشبار ونصف عرضها.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), I said: How much is the Kurr? He said: Three and a half spans in depth, by three and a half spans in width. Shaykh Hurr Amili: Mentioning the width suffices for mentioning the length because it must either equal or exceed it.

chapter: Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)
arabicText: اقل: سألت أاب عبد هللا عليه السالم عن الكر من الماء، كم يكون قدره؟ اقل: إذا كان الماء ثالثة أشبار ونصف في مثله ثالثة أشبار ونصف في عمقة في األرض فذلك الكر من الماء.
englishText: He said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Kurr of water, what is its measure? He said: When the water is three and a half spans by three and a half spans by its depth in the ground, that is the Kurr of water.

chapter: Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)
arabicText: عن بعض أصحابنا عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: الكر من الماء نحو حبي هذا، وأشار إلى حب من تلك الحباب التي تكون ابلمدينة.
englishText: From some of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Kurr of water is about the size of this water jar of mine, and he pointed to one of those water jars that are found in Medina. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The Sheikh said: "It is not improbable that the jar holds an amount of water equal to a Kurr."

chapter: Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: إذا كان الماء قدر قلتين لم ينجسه شئ، والقلتان جراتن.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: If the water reaches two qullahs nothing makes it impure, and the two qullahs are two jars. Shaykh Hurr Amili: Sheikh Saduq mentioned that it might be possible that this was mentioned under the pretext of taqiyyah, and it could be that the amount of the two Qullahs is the amount of a Kurr because a Qullah in the language refers to a large jar. In Al-Mu'tabar from Ibn AlJunayd who said: "A Kurr is two Qullahs, and its weight reaches 1200 pounds." And Ibn Durayd said: "The Qullah in the hadith is from 'Qalal of Hajar' and it is large, they claimed that one could hold five skins." The variation in hadiths regarding the measurement in cubits might be reconciled by considering the difference in water's weight, whether light or heavy, and the variation in the length of cubits, long or short, and considering the lesser amount as sufficient and the greater amount as preferred and precautionary. This was mentioned by a group of our scholars, and this is the closer opinion. And Allah knows best. Footnote: From the margin in the manuscript: All companions mentioned that the consideration for the Kurr is its crushed form, as 'fi' indicates 'to strike'. Mentioned by AlShahid and others. The first hadith can be reconciled with the second by considering the spherical form, where half of the radius is multiplied by half of the circumference, and the total is multiplied by the depth to reach twenty-seven. For if the circumference is nine cubits, then the diameter is three, which is its width. We multiply one and a half by four and a half, and the total by 4. The narration of three and a half cubits can also be considered in this manner, making the circumference 10 and a half. We multiply five and a quarter by one and three quarters, and the total by three and a half, so it does not exceed 30 except by a cubit, which approximates the other two narrations. Measure Of Kurr In Cubits (Ashbar)

chapter: Amount Of Kurr In Ratls
arabicText: عن أبي (عبد هللا عليه) السالم اقل: الكر من الماء الذي ال ينجسه شئ ألف ومأات رطل.
englishText: From Abu (Abdullah, peace be upon him) who said: The Kurr of water which nothing makes impure is one thousand and two hundred (Iraqi) ratls. Translator: Two Iraqi Ratls were equal to one Meccan Ratl.

chapter: Amount Of Kurr In Ratls
arabicText: عن عبد هللا بن المغيرة يرفعه إلى أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم أن الكر ستمأة رطل.
englishText: From Abdullah bin Al-Mughirah, raising it to Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, that the Kurr is six hundred ratls. Translator: One Ratl was 0.6 kg or 360 liters.

chapter: Amount Of Kurr In Ratls
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: والكر ستمأة رطل.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, said: And the Kurr is six hundred ratls. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The first narration intends the Iraqi pound, because it approximates the consideration of the cubits, and because they issued a fatwa to the questioner based on the custom of his country, and for that reason, the Sa' (a measure) was considered in the Iraqi pound, and because it aligns with the narration of six hundred, for the intended here is the Meccan pound, which is two Iraqi pounds. It is not permissible to mean by the six hundred the Iraqi or the Medinan pound, because it is abandoned by consensus, mentioned all by the Sheikh. And there will come in the narrations of added water what indicates their usage of the pound referring to the Iraqi pound, and there have been previously stated estimations for the Kurr all carried on the estimation by pounds or cubits, clear in their implications. And Allah knows best.

chapter: Obligation To Avoid Both Vessels When One Of Them Is Impure And They Are Mixed Up
arabicText: قد تقدم حديث سماعة، عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم في رجل معه إانءان، وقع في أحدهما قذر، وال يدري أيهما هو، وليس يقدر عىل ماء غيرهما، اقل: يهريقهما ويتيمم.
englishText: The hadith of Sama'ah has already preceded, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who has two vessels, and filth has fallen into one of them, and he does not know which one it is, and he does not have access to water other than these two. He (peace be upon him) said: He should pour out both of them and perform tayammum.

chapter: Impermissibility Of Using Impure Water For Purification, Even In Necessity, And Its Permissibility In Such Cases For Eating And Drinking Only  قد تقدم حديث عيل بن جعفر، عن أخيه موسى بن جعفر عليه السالم أنه سأله عن رجل رعف وهو يتوضأ فتقطر قطرة في إانئه، هل يصلح الوضوء منه؟ اقل: ال. The previous hadith of Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) has been mentioned, that he asked him about a man who got a nosebleed while performing ablution and a drop fell into his vessel, is it permissible to perform ablution from it? He said: No.
arabicText: وحديث سعيد األعرج أنه سأل أاب عبد هللا عليه السالم عن الجرة تسع مأة رطل، يقع فيها أوقية من دم، أشرب منه وأتوضأ؟ اقل: ال.
englishText: And the hadith of Sa'id Al-A'raj that he asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a jar containing nine hundred ratl (a unit of measurement), and an ounce of blood falls into it, can I drink from it and perform ablution? He said: No.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن الرضا (عليه السالم) اقل: ماء البئر واسع ال يفسده شئ إال أن يتغير به.
englishText: From Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said: Well water is expansive, nothing corrupts it except what changes it.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: سألته عن الحبل يكون من شعر الخنزير يستقى به الماء من البئر، هل يتوضأ من ذلك الماء؟ اقل: ال أبس.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him about the rope made of pig hair used to draw water from the well, can one perform ablution with that water? He said: There is no problem. Shaykh Hurr Amili: It appears that the intended water here is the water from the well, not the water in the bucket. If it means the water in the bucket, then the rope does not come into contact with it after being separated from the well, and it is possible that the bucket is considered as a large amount (kurr).

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم - في حديث - اقل: قلت له: الشعر الخنزير يعمل حبال ويستقى به من البئر التي يشرب منها أو يتوضأ منها؟ فقال: ال أبس به.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) - in a hadith - he said: I said to him: Pig hair made into a rope used to draw water from the well from which people drink or perform ablution? He said: There is no problem with it.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي الحسن عليه السالم في البئر يكون بينها وبين الكنيف خمس أذرع، أقل، أو أكثر، يتوضأ منها؟ اقل: ليس يكره من قرب وال بعد، يتوضأ منها ويغتسل ما لم يتغير الماء.
englishText: From Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a well that is five cubits or less or more from a latrine, can one perform ablution from it? He said: It is not disliked whether near or far, one can perform ablution and ritual bath from it as long as the water hasn't changed.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي بصير اقل: قلت ألبي عبد هللا عليه السالم، بئر يستقى منها، ويتوضئ به، وغسل منه الثياب، وعجن به، ثم علم أنه كان فيها ميت، اقل: ال أبس، وال يغسل منه الثوب، وال تعاد منه الصالة.
englishText: From Abu Basir who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding a well from which water is drawn, ablution is performed, clothes are washed, and dough is kneaded, then it becomes known that there was a dead body in it. He said: There is no problem, and the clothes need not be rewashed, nor should the prayers be repeated.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن الرضا عليه السالم اقل: ماء البئر واسع ال يفسده شئ إال أن يتغير ريحه، أو طعمه، فينزح حتى يذهب الريح، ويطيب طعمه ألن له مادة.
englishText: From Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said: Well water is expansive, nothing corrupts it except if its smell or taste changes, then it should be drawn until the smell disappears and its taste becomes good because it has a source.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: اقل: كتبت إلى رجل اسئله أن يسئل أاب الحسن الرضا (عليه السالم) فقال: ماء البئر واسع ال يفسده شئ إال أن يتغير ريحه، أو طعمه، فينزح منه حتى يذهب الريح ويطيب طعمه، ألن له مادة.
englishText: He said: I wrote to a man asking him to ask Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha (peace be upon him), and he said: Well water is expansive, nothing corrupts it except if its smell or taste changes, then water should be drawn from it until the smell disappears and its taste becomes good, because it has a source.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن موسى بن القاسم، عن عيل بن جعفر، عن أخيه موسى بن جعفر عليه السالم اقل: سألته عن بئر ماء وقع فيها زبيل من عذرة رطبة، أو ايبسة، أو زبيل من سرقين أيصلح الوضوء منها؟ اقل: ال أبس.
englishText: From Musa bin Al-Qasim, from Ali bin Ja'far, from his brother Musa bin Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a water well in which a basket of fresh or dry excrement, or a basket of dung falls, is it permissible to perform ablution from it? He said: There is no problem.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم في الفارة تقع في البئر، فيتوضأ الرجل منها، ويصيل وهو ال يعلم، أيعيد الصالة، ويغسل ثوبه؟ فقال: ال يعيد الصالة، وال يغسل ثوبه.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a mouse falling into a well, and a man performs ablution from it and prays while not knowing, should he repeat the prayer and wash his clothes? He said: He should not repeat the prayer, nor wash his clothes.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: سمعته يقول: ال يغسل الثوب، وال تعاد الصالة مما وقع في البئر إال أن ينتن، إفن أنتن غسل الثوب، وأعاد الصالة، ونزحت البئر.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: The clothes need not be washed, nor the prayer repeated due to what falls in the well unless it becomes putrid. If it becomes putrid, wash the clothes, repeat the prayer, and drain the well.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: سئل عن الفأرة تقع في البئر ال يعلم بها إال بعد ما يتوضأ منها، أيعاد الوضوء؟ فقال: ال.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a mouse falling into a well and it is not known until after performing ablution from it, should the ablution be repeated? He said: No.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: إذا وقع في البئر الطير والدجاجة والفأرة افنزح منها سبع دالء، قلنا: فما تقول: في صالتنا، ووضوئنا، وما أصاب ثيابنا؟ فقال: ال أبس به.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: If a bird, chicken, or mouse falls into the well, draw seven buckets from it. We said: What do you say about our prayers, ablution, and what touched our clothes? He said: There is no problem with it.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: سئل أبو عبد هللا عليه السالم عن الفارة تقع في البئر، اقل: إذا خرجت فال أبس، وإن تفسخت فسبع دالء، اقل: وسئل عن الفأرة تقع في البئر فال يعلم بها أحد إال بعد أن يتوضأ منها، أيعيد وضوئه، وصالته، ويغسل ما أصابه؟ فقال: ال، قد استعمل أهل الدار ورشوا، وفي رواية أخرى: قد استقى منها أهل الدار ورشوا.
englishText: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a mouse falling into the well. He said: If it comes out, there is no problem, and if it decomposes, then seven buckets. He was asked about a mouse falling into the well and no one knows about it until after performing ablution from it, should one repeat their ablution, prayer, and wash what was touched by it? He said: No, the household has already used it and sprinkled, and in another narration: the household has drawn from it and sprinkled. Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The ...

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: كنت مع أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم في طريق مكة فصران إلى بئر افستقى غالم أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم دلوا فخرج فيه أفراتن (١) فقال أبو عبد هللا عليه السالم: أرقه، افستقى آخر فخرج فيه أفرة، فقال: أبو عبد هللا عليه السالم أرقه، اقل: افستقى الثالث فلم يخرج فيه شئ، فقال: صبه في اإلانء. فصبه في االانء.
englishText: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) on the road to Makkah, and we came to a well. Abu Abdullah's servant drew a bucket and two mice came out in it. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Pour it out. He drew another and a mouse came out in it. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Pour it out. He drew a third and nothing came out in it, so he said: Pour it in the vessel. So he poured it in the vessel.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: سئل أبو عبد هللا عليه السالم عن البئر يقع فيها زبيل عذرة ايبسة أو رطبة، فقال: ال أبس إذا كان فيها ماء كثير.
englishText: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a well in which a basket of dry or fresh excrement falls, he said: There is no problem if there is abundant water in it.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا عليه السالم عن جلد الخنزير يجعل دلوا يستقى به الماء؟ اقل: ال أبس. اقل الشيخ: الوجه أنه ال أبس أن يستقى به، لكن يستعمل ذلك في سقي الدواب واألشجار ونحو ذلك.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, about using a pig's skin to make a bucket for drawing water? He said: There is no problem. The Shaykh said: The viewpoint is that there is no problem drawing water with it, but it should be used for watering animals, trees, and similar purposes.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا عليه السالم عن البئر يقع فيها الفارة أو غيرها من الدواب فتموت فيعجن من مائها، أيؤكل ذلك الخبز؟ اقل إذا أصابته النار فال أبس أبكله.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, about a well in which a mouse or other animals fall and die, and then its water is used for kneading dough, can that bread be eaten? He said: If it is touched by fire, there is no problem eating it.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم في عجين عجن وخبز، ثم علم أن الماء كانت فيه ميتة؟ اقل: ال أبس أكلت النار ما فيه.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, regarding dough that was kneaded and baked, then it was known that there was a dead animal in the water? He said: There is no problem, the fire consumed what was in it. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The water here is either what reaches the measure of a kurr, or well water, by inference from what was mentioned before and other [narrations]. The explanation is not to be taken literally, and there are many such examples. It could be considered that the touch of the fire removes the detestability of the dead [animal's] remnants.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: أنه سأل أاب جعفر عليه السالم عن سام أبرص وجدانه في البئر قد تفسخ؟ فقال: إنما عليك أن تنزح منها سبع دالء. فقال له: فثيابنا قد صلينا فيها نغسلها ونعيد الصالة؟ اقل: ال.
englishText: He asked Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, about a decomposed lizard we found in the well? He said: You only need to remove seven buckets of water from it. He asked him: Should we wash our clothes that we prayed in and repeat the prayers? He said: No. Shaykh Hurr Amili: It appears from this that drawing water does not indicate impurity, and there are similar cases that will be mentioned, God willing.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: اقل: واقل الصادق عليه السالم: كانت في المدينة بئر وسط مزبلة، فكانت الريح تهب وتلقى فيها القذر، وكان النبي صىل هللا عليه وآله وسلم يتوضأ منها.
englishText: He said: And Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: There was a well in Medina in the middle of a garbage dump, and the wind would blow and throw dirt into it, and the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, would perform ablution from it.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: كتبت إلى رجل أسأله أن يسأل أاب الحسن الرضا عليه السالم عن البئر تكون في المنزل للوضوء فيقطر فيها قطرت من بول أو دم، أو يسقط فيها شئ من عذرة كالبعرة ونحوها، ما الذي يطهرها حتى يحل الوضوء منها للصالة؟ فوقع عليه السالم بخطه في كتابي: ينزح دالء منها.
englishText: I wrote to a man asking him to ask Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha, peace be upon him, about a well in the house used for ablution, if drops of urine or blood fall into it, or something from excrement like dung and similar things falls into it, what purifies it so that ablution from it becomes permissible for prayer? He wrote in my letter in his handwriting: Draw several buckets from it. Shaykh Hurr Amili: From Muhammad bin Ismail, similarly, except that he said: "Or if something else falls into it like dung." I say: This report is among the doubts raised by those who argue that a well is affected by contact, and it is not explicit in that regard, for the implication of approval here is weak. It could be interpreted as cautionary, pertaining to cleanliness in the conventional sense, recommending avoidance before drawing water, aimed at eliminating the possibility of change and dispelling repulsion, among other interpretations. The generality in this and in the reports about drawing water is an indication of recommendation, Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The ... with considerable differences as you can see, including the established practice of drawing water without impurity, such as the case of a person in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), or things that do not have a flowing blood, and explicit statements allowing use before drawing water, among other points.

chapter: Non-Impurity Of Well Water By Mere Contact Without Change, And The Ruling On Drawing Water
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا عليه السالم اقل: إذا أتيت البئر وأنت جنب فلم تجد دلوا وال شيئا تغرف به، فتيمم ابلصعيد إفن رب الماء رب الصعيد، وال تقع في البئر، وال تفسد عىل القوم مائهم.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah, peace be upon him, who said: If you come to a well while you are in a state of major ritual impurity and you don't find a bucket or anything to draw water with, then perform tayammum with earth, for the Lord of water is the Lord of earth, and do not enter the well, and do not spoil the people's water. Shaykh Hurr Amili: This too has been used as evidence for impurity, but its weakness is apparent because there's a clear indication that the allowance for tayammum is due to the lack of access to water, and the reason for prohibiting spoiling is related to the disturbance caused by falling into it, which stirs up the sediment (sludge), and in terms of drinking or the like, spoiling, which is broader than impurity, hence it does not indicate impurity. Contrarily, in the report from Muhammad bin Ismail, spoiling, with its general scope, encompasses impurity unless it specifically meant it. This is supported by the fact that there's no explicit mention of impurity on the body of the person in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), thus it's determined that the spoiling mentioned refers to what was stated, or the occurrence of repulsion, or hastening of change, or the prohibition of falling into it due to the risk and exposure to destruction that rapidly spoils the water if one were to die in it. With these possibilities and more, the argument does not hold, and the reports about purification are clearer in indication and farther from taqiyyah, indeed without any contest upon thorough investigation, supported by reports on the purity of water, reports on change, reports on flowing water since it is a part of it, interpreted as gushing whether it flows or not, and reports on the kurr (a certain measure of water) because it is generally a kurr, and reports on the source and more. Previously mentioned reports indicated the consideration of kurr in well water, and the sheikh attributed it to taqiyyah.

chapter: Amount Of Water To Be Drawn From The Well For The Death Of An Ox, Donkey, Camel, Wine, And Intoxicants, And The Spillage Of Wine
arabicText: عن عبد هللا بن سنان، عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: إن سقط في البئر دابة صغيرة، أو نزل فيها جنب، نزح منها سبع دالء، إفن مات فيها ثور، أو صب فيها خمر، نزح الماء كله.
englishText: Abdullah bin Sinan narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: If a small animal falls into a well, or a person in a state of major ritual impurity descends into it, seven buckets should be drawn from it. If a bull dies in it, or wine is poured into it, all the water should be drawn out.

chapter: Amount Of Water To Be Drawn From The Well For The Death Of An Ox, Donkey, Camel, Wine, And Intoxicants, And The Spillage Of Wine
arabicText: سألت أاب الحسن (عليه السالم) عن البئر يقع فيها قطرة دم، أو نبيذ مسكر، أو بول، أو خمر؟ اقل: ينزح منها ثالثون دلوا.
englishText: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a well in which a drop of blood, or intoxicating nabidh, or urine, or wine falls? He said: Thirty buckets should be drawn from it.

chapter: Amount Of Water To Be Drawn From The Well For The Death Of An Ox, Donkey, Camel, Wine, And Intoxicants, And The Spillage Of Wine
arabicText: قلت ألبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم): بئر قطرت فيها قطرة دم، أو خمر، اقل: الدم والخمر والميت ولحم الخنزير ذلك كله واحد، ينزح منه عشرون دلوا، إفن غلب الريح نزحت حتى تطيب.
englishText: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A well into which a drop of blood or wine fell. He said: Blood, wine, carrion, and pork are all the same in this regard. Twenty buckets should be drawn from it. If the odor persists, continue drawing until it becomes pure.

chapter: Amount Of Water To Be Drawn From The Well For The Death Of An Ox, Donkey, Camel, Wine, And Intoxicants, And The Spillage Of Wine
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) في البئر يبول فيها الصبي، أو يصب فيها بول، أو خمر، فقال: ينزح الماء كله.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding a well into which a child urinates, or urine is poured, or wine is poured, he said: All the water must be drawn out.

chapter: Amount Of Water To Be Drawn From The Well For The Death Of An Ox, Donkey, Camel, Wine, And Intoxicants, And The Spillage Of Wine
arabicText: سألت أاب جعفر (عليه السالم) عما يقع في البئر ما بين الفارة والسنور إلى الشاة؟ فقال: كل ذلك نقول: سبع دالء. ، اقل: حتى بلغت الحمار والجمل؟ فقال: كر من ماء. اقل: وأقل ما يقع في البئر عصفور ينزح منها دلو واحد.
englishText: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what falls into the well, ranging from a mouse to a cat to a sheep? He said: For all of these, we say: seven buckets. I said: Even up to a donkey and a camel? He said: A kurr of water. He said: And the least that falls into the well, such as a sparrow, requires drawing one bucket.

chapter: Amount Of Water To Be Drawn From The Well For The Death Of An Ox, Donkey, Camel, Wine, And Intoxicants, And The Spillage Of Wine
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: إذا سقط في البئر شئ صغير فمات فيها افنزح منها دالء، وإن وقع فيها جنب افنزح منها سبع دالء وإن مات فيها بعير، أو صب فيها خمر فلتنزح.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: If a small thing falls into a well and dies in it, then draw buckets from it. If a person in a state of major ritual impurity falls into it, then draw seven buckets from it. And if a camel dies in it, or wine is poured into it, then it should be completely emptied. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The Sheikh narrated it with his chain from Muhammad bin Ya'qub, and added to it: "then all the water should be drawn out." A group of our scholars mentioned that the lesser amount mentioned in this chapter and others is based on parts, and the greater amount on preference.

chapter: What Is Drawn From The Well For The Urination Of A Child, A Man, And Others
arabicText: حدثني عدة، عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: ينزح منه سبع دالء إذا ابل فيها الصبي، أو وقعت فيها أفرة أو نحوها.
englishText: A group narrated to me, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Seven buckets should be drawn from it if a child urinates in it, or if a mouse or something similar falls into it.

chapter: What Is Drawn From The Well For The Urination Of A Child, A Man, And Others
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: سألته عن بول الصبي الفطيم يقع في البئر، فقال: دلو واحد. قلت: بول الرجل، اقل: ينزح منها أربعون دلوا.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him about the urine of a weaned child falling into a well, so he said: One bucket [is to be drawn out]. I said: [What about] a man's urine? He said: Forty buckets are to be drawn out from it.

chapter: What Is Drawn From The Well For The Urination Of A Child, A Man, And Others
arabicText: سألت أاب الحسن (عليه السالم) عن بئر يدخلها ماء المطر فيه البول، والعذرة وأبوال الدواب، وأرواثها، وخرؤ الكالب؟ اقل: ينزح منها ثالثون دلوا، وإن كانت مبخرة.
englishText: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a well into which rainwater enters containing urine, excrement, animal urine, animal dung, and dog feces. He said: Thirty buckets should be drawn from it, even if it has a foul odor.

chapter: What Is Drawn From The Well For The Urination Of A Child, A Man, And Others
arabicText: اقل: االخبار متواترة عن األئمة الطاهرة (عليهم السالم) أبن ينزح لبول االنسان أربعون دلوا.
englishText: He said: The reports are abundantly narrated from the pure Imams (peace be upon them) that forty buckets should be drawn for human urine.

chapter: What Is Drawn From The Well For The Urination Of A Child, A Man, And Others
arabicText: عن أبي الحسن (عليه السالم) في البئر يقع فيها قطرة دم، أو نبيذ مسكر، أو بول، أخمر، اقل: ينزح منها ثالثون دلوا.
englishText: From Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a well into which falls a drop of blood, or intoxicating wine, or urine, or wine, he said: Thirty buckets should be drawn from it.

chapter: What Is Drawn From The Well For The Urination Of A Child, A Man, And Others
arabicText: عن الرضا (عليه السالم) في البئر يقطر فيها قطرات من بول أو دم: اقل: ينزح منها دالء.
englishText: From Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) regarding a well into which drops of urine or blood have fallen: He said: Several buckets should be drawn from it.

chapter: What Is Drawn From The Well For The Urination Of A Child, A Man, And Others
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) في البئر يبول فيها الصبي، أو يصب فيها بول، أو خمر، اقل: ينزح الماء كله. أقول: حمله الشيخ عىل حصول التغير، وحمل حديث عيل بن أبي حمزة عىل الصبي الذي لم أيكل الطعام، واقل غيره: إن األقل يجزي، واألكثر أفضل.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a well in which a child urinates, or urine is poured into it, or wine, he said: All the water should be drawn out. I (Hurr Amili) say: The Shaykh interpreted this to mean when a change occurs, and he interpreted the hadith of Ali bin Abi Hamza as referring to a child who has not yet eaten solid food. Others said: Drawing out a small amount suffices, but drawing out more is preferable.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: كان أبو جعفر (عليه السالم) يقول: إذا مات الكلب في البئر نزحت. واقل أبو جعفر (عليه السالم) إذا وقع فيها ثم اخرج منها حيا نزح منها سبع دالء.
englishText: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: When a dog dies in a well, it should be emptied. And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: If it falls into it and then is taken out alive, seven buckets should be drawn from it. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The Sheikh interpreted the drawing off of everything to be due to change.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: عن أبي الحسن موسى بن جعفر (عليه السالم) اقل: سألته عن البئر تقع فيها الحمامة، والدجاجة، والفأرة أو الكلب، أو الهرة؟ فقال: يجزيك أن تنزح منها دالء، إفن ذلك يطهرها إنشاء هللا تعالى.
englishText: From Abu Al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a well into which a pigeon, or a chicken, or a mouse, or a dog, or a cat falls? He said: It suffices you to draw some buckets of water from it, for that will purify it, insha'Allah.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الفأرة تقع في البئر؟ فقال سبع دالء. وسألته عن الطير، والدجاجة، تقع في البئر؟ اقل: سبع دالء، والسنور عشرون، أو ثالثون. أو أربعون دلوا، والكلب وشبهه.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a mouse falling into a well? He said: Seven buckets. And I asked him about a bird and a chicken falling into the well? He said: Seven buckets. And for a cat, twenty, or thirty, or forty buckets, and the same for a dog and similar animals.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: اقل سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الفارة تقع في البئر، أو الطير؟ اقل: إن أدركته قبل أن ينتن نزحت منها سبع دالء، وإن كانت سنورا أو أكبر منه نزحت منها ثالثين دلوا، أو أربعين دلوا، وإن أنتن حتى يوجد ريح النتن في الماء نزحت البئر حتى يذهب النتن من الماء.
englishText: He said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a mouse or a bird falling into a well? He said: If you catch it before it rots, draw seven buckets from it. If it is a cat or larger, draw thirty or forty buckets from it. If it rots until the smell of decay is found in the water, draw from the well until the stench is gone from the water.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا و أبى جعفر (عليهما السالم) في البئر تقع فيها الدابة، والفارة، والكلب، والخنزير، والطير فيموت، اقل: يخرج ثم ينزح من البئر دالء ثم اشرب منه، وتوضأ.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them) regarding a well into which an animal, a mouse, a dog, a pig, or a bird falls and dies, they said: Remove it, then draw several buckets from the well, then drink from it and perform ablution.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: اقل أبو عبد هللا (عليه السالم): في البئر يقع فيها الفارة أو الدابة، أو الكلب، أو الطير فيموت، اقل: يخرج ثم ينزح من البئر دالء ثم يشرب منه ويتوضأ.
englishText: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding a well into which a mouse, an animal, a dog, or a bird falls and dies, he said: Remove it, then draw several buckets of water from the well, then one may drink from it and perform ablution.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) في الفأرة، والسنور، والدجاجة، والكلب، والطير، اقل: إفذا لم يتفسخ، أو يتغير طعم الماء، فيكفيك خمس دالء وإن تغير الماء فخذ منه حتى تذهب الريح.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding the mouse, cat, chicken, dog, and bird, he said: If it has not decomposed, or the taste of the water has not changed, then five buckets are sufficient for you. And if the water has changed, then take from it until the odor disappears.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: سئل عن بئر يقع فيها كلب، أو افرة، أو خنزير؟ اقل: تنزح كلها.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: He was asked about a well into which a dog, or a rat, or a pig falls? He said: Remove all its water.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: الدم، والخمر، والميت ولحم الخنزير، في ذلك كله واحد ينزح منها عشرون دلوا.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Blood, wine, carrion, and pork - in all of these cases the ruling is the same - twenty buckets must be drawn out [from the well that has been contaminated with any of these].

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: وحديث عمرو بن سعيد، عن أبي جعفر (عليه السالم) أنه ينزح للسنور سبع دالء.
englishText: The hadith of Amr ibn Sa'id, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that seven buckets should be drawn for a cat.

chapter: On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عما يقع في اآلابر؟ فقال: أما الفأرة وأشباهها فينزح منها سبع دالء، إال أن يتغير الماء فينزح حتى يطيب، إفن سقط فيها كلب فقدرت أن تنزح ماءها اففعل، وكل شئ وقع في البئر ليس له دم مثل العقرب، والخنافس، وأشباه ذلك فال أبس.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about what falls into wells? He said: As for mice and similar creatures, seven buckets should be drawn out, unless the water changes then keep drawing until it becomes pure. If a dog falls in and you are able to draw out all its water then do so. And everything that falls into the well that has no blood, like scorpions, beetles and similar things, then there is no problem. On What Is To Be Drawn From A Well For Cats, Dogs, Pigs, And The Like

chapter: Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Similar Cases
arabicText: سألته عن الفأرة تقع في البئر، أو الطير؟ اقل: إن أدركته أن ينتن نزحت منها سبع دالء.
englishText: I asked him about a mouse or bird falling into a well? He said: If you find it before it decays, draw out seven buckets.

chapter: Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Similar Cases
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الفأرة تقع في البئر؟ اقل: سبع دالء. اقل: وسألته عن الطير والدجاجة تقع في البئر؟ اقل: سبع دالء.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a mouse falling into a well? He said: Seven buckets. He said: And I asked him about a bird or chicken falling into a well? He said: Seven buckets.

chapter: Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Similar Cases
arabicText: عن جعفر، عن أبيه (عليه السالم) أن عليا (عليه السالم) كان يقول: الدجاجة ومثلها تموت في البئر ينزح منها دلوان، أو ثالثة، إفذا كانت شاة أو ما أشبهها فتسعة أو عشرة.
englishText: From Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him) that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: When a chicken or something similar dies in a well, draw two or three buckets from it, and if it is a sheep or something similar then draw nine or ten buckets.

chapter: Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Similar Cases
arabicText: وقد تقدم في حديث عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم): في الدابة الصغيرة سبع دالء.
englishText: And it was previously mentioned in a hadith from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): For a small animal, draw seven buckets.

chapter: Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Similar Cases
arabicText: وعنه (عليه السالم) إذا وقع في البئر الطير، والدجاجة، والفأرة، افنزح منها سبع دالء.
englishText: And from him (peace be upon him): When a bird, chicken, or mouse falls into the well, draw seven buckets from it.

chapter: Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Similar Cases
arabicText: وعنه (عليه السالم) في العصفور دلو واحد.
englishText: From him (peace be upon him): For a sparrow, one bucket.

chapter: Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Similar Cases
arabicText: وعن أبي جعفر (عليه السالم) في الشاة سبع دالء.
englishText: From Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): For a sheep, seven buckets.

chapter: Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Similar Cases
arabicText: وعن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) في الطير خمس دالء.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): For a bird, five buckets. Amount To Be Drawn Out For A Chicken, Pigeon, Bird, Sheep And Simil...

chapter: What Is Drawn For A Mouse, Gecko, Poisonous Lizard, Scorpion, And The Like
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: إذا وقعت الفأرة في البئر فتسلخت افنزح منها سبع دالء. وفى رواية أخرى فتفسخت.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: If a mouse falls into a well and its skin peels off, then draw seven buckets from it. And in another narration: and it decomposes.

chapter: What Is Drawn For A Mouse, Gecko, Poisonous Lizard, Scorpion, And The Like
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الفأرة، والوزغة تقع في البئر، اقل: ينزح منها ثالث دالء.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a mouse and a gecko falling into a well. He said: Draw three buckets of water from it.

chapter: What Is Drawn For A Mouse, Gecko, Poisonous Lizard, Scorpion, And The Like
arabicText: سألت أاب عبد هللا (عليه السالم) عن الفأرة تقع في البئر، اقل: سبع دالء.
englishText: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a mouse falling into a well. He said: Seven buckets. Shaykh Hurr Amili: The Sheikh said: What entails seven buckets is carried on the condition that it has decomposed, and three if it has not decomposed as mentioned before.

chapter: What Is Drawn For A Mouse, Gecko, Poisonous Lizard, Scorpion, And The Like
arabicText: عن أبي عبد هللا (عليه السالم) اقل: سئل عن الفأرة تقع في البئر اقل: إذا ماتت ولم تنتن أفربعين دلوا، وإذا انتفخت فيه ونتنت نزح الماء كله.
englishText: From Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: He was asked about a mouse falling into a well. He said: If it dies and does not become putrid, then draw forty buckets. And if it swells and becomes putrid in it, then draw out all the water.
